en.title: Enroll device {name}
en.note: Use one of the links or commands on the device. The downloaded installer enrolls the device when it runs; the manual commands are for a device that already has the client. When enrollment finishes, the device appears in the device table by itself; then add mappings for it on its device page.
en.winHelp: Open the link in a browser on the Windows device and run the downloaded file; it enrolls the device by itself. If SmartScreen warns about an unknown publisher, choose More info, then Run anyway.
en.linuxHelp: Paste this line into a shell on the device (for example over SSH). It downloads the installer, installs the client and enrolls the device by itself.
en.pinHelp: -k skips the system certificate check and --pinnedpubkey accepts only this server's public key, so a self-signed certificate is still protected against a man in the middle.
en.wgetHelp: Without curl, use wget; its SHA-256 check refuses a changed file.
en.linkHelp: Or download it in a browser, then run it with sh:
en.noPkg: This server has no {os} installer package.
en.noPkgNote: This server has no client installer packages. To offer them here, put them on the server with kaze-syncd client-pkg. Until then use the manual commands below.
en.verDiff: A client package on this server differs from the server version {server}. It still works while the protocols are compatible; to use the server's version, replace the packages with kaze-syncd client-pkg.

ma.title: Add mapping
ma.note: If the directory does not exist, the client creates it. If it is not empty and is not already a synced directory, reconciliation starts only when "Allow adopting a non-empty directory" is ticked (for moving over from another sync tool). This keeps a path mistyped as a whole home directory from being uploaded in full.

me.help: Changing the path is the same as deleting the old mapping and adding a new one: the files at the old path stay as they are, and the new path is reconciled afresh.

notice.wc.unset: No write rules are set yet; the root is single writer by default
advice.wc.unset: Any writer: several devices share the writing; when two change the same file, only that file is frozen. Single writer: one device writes at a time, right for directories that must stay consistent as a whole such as git repositories; on a simultaneous write the device that came second is frozen for the whole scope. Exclusive: only the named device may write. The root is single writer by default: when a device that is often offline comes back and another device has changed the folder meanwhile, its sync of the whole folder is frozen until you decide here. For folders of unrelated files set the root to any writer and make only repositories and the like single writer.
wc.tip.file: Each file here is a single-writer scope of its own.

dlg.wc.title: Write control
dlg.wc.free: Any writer: devices share the writing
dlg.wc.free.help: When two devices change one file, only that file is frozen.
dlg.wc.single: Single writer: one device writes at a time
dlg.wc.single.help: A simultaneous write, or one based on stale content, freezes the device that came second for the whole scope.
dlg.wc.exclusive: Exclusive: only the named device writes
dlg.wc.exclusive.help: Any change from another device freezes its sync of the scope.
dlg.wc.root: The root is single writer by default. When a device that is often offline comes back and another device has changed the folder meanwhile, its sync of the whole folder is frozen until you decide; for folders of unrelated files choose "Any writer".
dlg.wc.sub: Rules of subdirectories and files are set in the context menu of the file list (or the ⋯ at the end of a row).
set.windowNote: In a single-writer scope, a write by another device within this long after one reached the server counts as simultaneous; 0 means no window: only writes based on stale content count.

js.push.insecure: This device does not trust the server's certificate, so this page is not a secure context and the browser does not allow push. Import the CA certificate on this device (user manual, section 2.4), then open this page again at an address the certificate covers.

js.push.saveFail: The server did not complete this ({code}). Try again later.
js.push.noService: The browser could not reach its push service (Google's FCM on Android Chrome). A phone without Google Play services, or one that cannot reach Google, cannot receive Web Push here. Check that Google Play services is installed and the phone can reach the internet, then try again.

js.push.offDone: Push is off in this browser.
